pr.title: Plan instrument knobs: choose with the arrows, turn with up and down, and record every turn
pr.head: fd53df5d0887acf92d91cfcb05ca76e5df3953f9

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a MIDI instrument. It publishes a virtual MIDI source, Field Keys, and, given an instrument such as juno, starts a voice host: a SuperCollider process that turns each note into a voice of that instrument. Today the only part of the sound you can change while you play is the modulation wheel, in six fixed steps on keys 3 to 8. Everything else, such as juno's filter cutoff, is a constant in the instrument's program, so changing it means editing the file and saving.

This pull request adds a plan, docs/projects/instrument-knobs/readme.md, at status: ready and priority: next. It changes no code. After Justin's review, the plan makes field keys a MIDI controller with knobs. A small YAML knob file beside each instrument, or one you name with --knobs, lists the knobs: each one's name, MIDI controller number, range, curve, and default. field keys checks the file, shows the knobs on a line of their own, and sends every change as an ordinary control change, so Logic or a hardware synth can answer it as well as juno.

A SuperCollider voice answers through the voicer, which hands each controller to the voice as a control named for its number, cc74, from 0 to 1. The voice maps that control to its own parameter, reading a copy of its knob file that Field wrote after the file passed its checks. The environment variable FIELD_KNOBS names the copy. A new default keymap, musical, puts choosing and turning on the arrows, typing a value on the number row, and the pitch bend on , and .. Esc cancels a typed value and no longer quits, and Ctrl-C quits.

Five reviews have read this plan. The first two found three defects, and all are fixed. The later three found it clean. At this head, Justin moved the bend to , and ., so . types the decimal point only while a value is being typed. One call in §3.2, that a voice reads the checked copy rather than writing its ranges a second time, is recommended and awaits Justin's ruling.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Knob file: <program>.knobs.yaml beside an instrument, or a file named with --knobs. It lists each knob's name, cc, min, max, curve, step, units, and default.
  • Controller (CC): a MIDI control-change number from 0 to 127. CC 1 is the modulation wheel, shown as the knob mod, and CC 64 is the sustain pedal.
  • cc<n>: the control the voicer sets on every voice for controller n, from 0 to 1, as it sets mod for the wheel today.
  • FIELD_KNOBS: the environment variable that names the checked copy of an instrument's knob file, which is the only knob file a SuperCollider voice reads.
  • Voicer: sc/voicer.scd, the MIDI-to-voice rules that the live voice host and a take's offline render share.
  • musical: the new default keymap, Field's adaptation of Logic's Musical Typing, which replaces musical-typing.
  • Entry and glide: a value you type on the number row, with . as its decimal point, and the run of control changes that moves the knob to it at the keymap's glide speed.
  • Chase: the daemon remembering each controller's last value before a take starts, so the take can start with it.

cards.title: Review history
cards.html:
• First review (19ff3ed), fixed. Two open questions waited on Justin in a ready plan, and criterion 1's res width contradicted §2.5.
  • Second review (6109c84), fixed. The voice and a take's render read the knob file unchecked, so a file field keys rejected still shaped the sound. Every path now checks the file first, and a voice reads only a copy that passed.
  • Third review (05e75dd), clean. Suggestions: put field check's knob check in the voice render's validate, name FIELD_KNOBS in docs/keys.md, and rewrap two paragraphs.
  • Fourth review (f6a6bba), clean, incremental. The push takes the three suggestions, and the knob check in the voice render's validate stops a bad file before sclang runs, because field build refuses a project with errors first.
  • Fifth review (fd53df5), clean. A full review of Justin's move of the bend to , and ., and of Period typing the decimal point only during an entry.

cards.title: Three chunks
cards.html:
1. Knobs, live and in takes. Knob files and --knobs, choosing and turning, the knob line, musical with the bend on , and ., the voicer's cc<n>, the checked copies a voice reads, the render's check, field check, and juno and bass with their knob files.
  2. Typing and the glide. The number row, Enter, Backspace, Period as the decimal point during an entry, Esc cancelling instead of quitting, and the keymap's glide.
  3. Where a take starts. .field/keys.json, controllers in the daemon's arm request, and the daemon's chase.

cards.title: Deferred out of the plan
cards.html:
• Knobs in the Electron UI, until the UI plays instruments (arming.md chunk 3).
  • Knob keys in tracker and fourths, until musical has been played with.
  • Finer than 128 steps, until a knob's steps are audible.
  • Saving a dialed-in sound, until someone wants to keep one.

groups.title: The instrument knobs plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: knob files, a knob line in field keys, typing and gliding values, and takes that keep every change
intro: The plan follows the repository's plan layout. §1 states the problem, §2 the design, §3 the decisions with the alternatives they beat, §4 the acceptance criteria and tests, §5 the cost, §6 the three chunks, §7 the questions deferred out of the plan, and §8 the facts about today's code the design rests on.

The design keeps knob logic in one place. field keys reads and checks the knob files in TypeScript, keeps each knob's value, and sends only MIDI control changes. Everything downstream already handles control changes: the daemon records them into a take, the take's render replays them through the voicer, and the voicer, which sets mod from the wheel today, sets cc<n> for every other controller. A SuperCollider voice maps cc<n> to its parameter itself, from a copy of its knob file that passed the same TypeScript check, so no SuperCollider code validates anything.
Read §2.2 for the knob file, §2.3 for the musical keymap, §2.4 for how an instrument answers, §2.5 for what you see, §2.7 for typing and gliding, and §3.1 for the calls Justin made in review.

checks.text: Every section the plan cites exists and says what the plan cites it for: keyboard-instrument.md §2.2, §2.3, §2.4, §2.6, §3, §5, §14, and §14.5, and arming.md chunk 3. Checked by reading each section at the base.

Every reference to musical-typing outside the plans sits in a file §2.9 lists or a test §4 names: docs/keys.md, bass.scd's comment, src/cli.ts, DEFAULT_KEYMAP in src/keys/keymap.ts, and five test files. Checked with git grep at the head.

Three open pull requests, #196, #198, and #201, touch files this plan will change, such as sc/voice-host.scd, src/commands/keys.ts, and the daemon's player.cpp. They overlap in text only. #201 gives each instrument's synths their own output bus and leaves the voices' controls alone.

files.note: The new plan, at status: ready and priority: next, revised after Justin's review and two review rounds.

checks.text: The heading has no Plan: prefix, which matches every plan on main since #200 merged. Checked with git grep on main.
The entry is padded to cutoff's width of eight characters, cutoff 800_ Hz, as §2.5's rule gives. Recomputed.

A save that fails changes only the status line: field keys keeps the last good list, keeps the voice's copy as it was, and sends no reload. Criterion 11 and the keys.test.ts bullet check it. This fixes the second review's finding.

juno's defaults here (2000, 0.3, 0.8, 1.5) are the constants in juno.scd's settings Event, and each sits inside its range. bass's attack default, 0.005, is the bottom of its range, which the rule on line 172 allows.
These formulas are SuperCollider's ControlSpec.map: it clips to 0 to 1, applies the warp, and rounds to step. Checked in SuperCollider 3.14.1's Spec.sc.

Every path that hands a knob file to an instrument now runs this schema first: field keys at start and on each save, and the voice render's validate. loadProject runs that validate for every record entry's instrument, and field build refuses a project with errors before it renders, so a bad file stops the render before sclang runs and field check reports the same error. Traced in src/model/project.ts and src/commands/build.ts.
SuperCollider's ExponentialWarp maps with (max / min) ** x * min, so a range with min 0 gives nan for every value above 0. That is why this rule exists. Checked in Spec.sc.
musical-typing.yaml plays notes on the home row and W E T Y U O P, so the arrows, Comma, Period, and Minus are free for these bindings. All three are positions src/keys/position.ts already knows.

tracker plays notes on Comma and Period, but it binds no type action, so no entry can open there and . stays a note in it. musical keeps musical-typing's notes, which use neither key. Checked in keymaps/.

The repository's YAML library reads type: 1 as the number 1, and the action table and the keymap test take a digit as a number from 0 to 9. "." is no longer a type value, because Period types the decimal point only during an entry.

The voicer today turns CC 1 into mod, handles CC 64 and CC 123, and ignores every other controller. Its start callback takes four arguments, so passing each cc<n> to a new voice is new. Checked in sc/voicer.scd.

The copy is what makes a failed save harmless. The voice reads FIELD_KNOBS, which field keys rewrites only after a save passes, so even a save of juno.scd while its knob file fails loads the last good copy.

This helper works in SuperCollider 3.14.1. A scratch program built a SynthDef with it and got controls cc74 and cc71 at the unmapped defaults, 0.647 and 0.316. parseYAMLFile returned the numbers as strings, as the text says. This head changes only where the file's path comes from.
Recomputed from §2.5's rules over all 128 controller values: mod pads to 3, cutoff to 8, res to 5 (0.000 to 0.950), and attack and release to 7. That gives this line exactly, and criterion 1's.
From 0, one step at the press, then 18, 24, and 84 steps through §2.6's bands, reach 127 at 2.30 s, at no more than 25 control changes a second.

KeysSession.release acts on heldControls, which records what each press did. So a Period press that began a bend ends it on release, and one that typed . releases nothing, whichever way the entry changed while the key was held. Checked in src/keys/session.ts.
Recomputed: 800 Hz is nearest controller value 62 (809.6 Hz, shown as 810 Hz), 99999 clamps to 127, and 20 clamps to 0. ControlSpec(50, 15000, \exp).map(62 / 127) is 809.6 in sclang.
At glide: 1, 127 steps a second is about 5 steps a 40 ms tick, so 127 to 62 takes 13 ticks, 520 ms, which matches "half a second" and the session test.

Today isQuit in src/keys/terminal.ts quits on Esc and on Ctrl-C, and the keymap schema refuses Escape because "it always quits". This plan changes both and amends keyboard-instrument.md §2.4, where that rule lives.
Rows in arrival order answer the first review's suggestion. The voicer keeps one value per controller for every channel, so the render ends on whichever value arrived last, as the live voice did.

verifyAfterRun already exists on the voice render and refuses to cache a render whose program changed while it ran. Its validate is already what field check calls for each record entry's instrument, so putting the knob check there makes check and build share one rule, as they do for the program.
This row now names FIELD_KNOBS under "Make an instrument playable", where an instrument's author reads the voice contract, as the docs/build-graph.md row below it does.

This call awaits Justin's ruling, but the plan answers it: §2.4, §2.9, the criteria, and the tests all build the checked copy, and the alternative of writing each range twice is recorded here. So the readiness of a ready plan does not hang on it.
A call made for Justin's review, with the two alternatives it beat. The cost it accepts is that a value starts with 0, not ., and that the bend up waits while a value is being typed.
Criterion 1's knob line matches §2.5's rules, recomputed. This was the first review's second finding.
This criterion checks the build path of the second review's finding: a knob file with an exp range at 0 fails field check and the take's render, instead of rendering a nan cutoff.
0.8 on attack, ControlSpec(0.005, 4, \exp), lands on controller value 96, which prints 782 ms. Recomputed.
Criterion 20 now turns cutoff down instead of typing a value, so chunk 3 needs only chunk 1, as stated. The rollout assigns each of the 22 criteria to a chunk.
Every question below is deferred out of the plan, with what reopens it, so the ready status holds. This was the first review's first finding.
positionOf in src/keys/position.ts maps only codes 9 (Tab) and 32 (Space) among functional keys, so Enter and Backspace resolve to nothing today, as stated.
